scope: Choose a persisted workflow for consequential dependencies or resumable work.

instruction_changes.deviation: The former standing rule asked agents to use Dynamic Workflows when useful without identifying the point at which a decision is needed.
instruction_changes.evidence: The user asked the agent to make the selection on its own and explicitly requested an update to the rule.
instruction_changes.why_instruction: The decision precedes dispatch and applies across tasks and hosts.
instruction_changes.alternative: Keep ordinary parallel execution for work that can be integrated in the current turn without a consequential dependency.

user_preference.request: Update the standing rule so the agent chooses when to use Dynamic Workflows on its own.
user_preference.scope: Workflow selection before dispatch, revision-bound check results, and fallback when the route is unavailable.

change_reconciliation.authority: Explicit user preference to clarify and update the existing orchestration rule.
change_reconciliation.requirement_reason: Specify when to choose a persisted workflow within the existing authorization and resource limits.
change_reconciliation.checks: Canonical renderer check across Codex, Hermes, and OMP; nine rendering tests and eleven direct-preference tests.

outcome_review.expected: Each managed overlay carries the same pre-dispatch trigger, ordinary parallel path, and dependency-preserving fallback.
outcome_review.observed: The canonical renderer generated and checked the three host overlays, and the existing rendering and direct-preference tests passed.
outcome_review.evidence: Rendered recovery overlays and the renderer and preference tests.
outcome_review.limitations: Checks establish source, projection, and preference acceptance; live workflow routing was outside the test.

obligations.reason: Define the explicit selection rule at its shared owner.
Record the user's autonomous workflow selection requirement.

Host execution routes, prerequisites, and portability remain governed by the existing matrix.
The existing method for measuring total cost remains applicable to the execution choice.
